title: Primary GRPO Reward: Leverage vs. Wiggum Scalar
question: Does leverage (score × output_lines / runtime_hours) capture quality that the wiggum scalar misses — specifically, does it penalize verbose but shallow runs that score well?
hypothesis: Kendall-tau(leverage_rank, score_rank) > 0.80 across rollouts, meaning they agree on most ranking decisions; but leverage identifies 10-20% of rollouts as over-verbose where score > 7.0 and output_lines > 300.
falsified_if: Kendall-tau < 0.65 (systematic disagreement too large to ignore) OR no runs found where score >= 7.0 and leverage is bottom-quartile (leverage penalty never fires meaningfully).

decision_rule.use_score_only: Kendall-tau >= 0.85 AND verbose_outliers < 5% of rollouts — leverage adds noise, not signal
decision_rule.use_leverage_only: Kendall-tau < 0.65 — systematic disagreement; inspect manually before deciding

method.note: Full wiggum revision enabled (NOT --score-only). Leverage computed from runs.jsonl: score * output_lines / (run_duration_s / 3600). Reuses checkpoint from Exp A if tasks overlap; only re-runs if checkpoint missing.

outputs: kendall_tau_overall.json — single tau across all rollout pairs
verbose_outliers.json — rollouts where score>=7.0 and leverage in bottom 25%
reward_ranking_comparison.json — rank order diff between score-only and combined reward per task

controlled.tasks: same 20 tasks as Exp A — shared checkpoint DB

requires: collect_rl_data.py: emit leverage per completion in grpo.jsonl (score * output_lines / runtime_hours)
leverage field must be sourced from runs.jsonl run_duration_s + final_content line count
code_note: In emit_grpo(), for each rollout compute: lines = len(content.splitlines()); runtime_h = run_data.get('run_duration_s', 1) / 3600; leverage = score * lines / max(runtime_h, 0.001). Add to completion dict.
